headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can read/write shared VS Code files while dbt-core can act on warehouse data, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and uses MCP; dbt-core can consume project files and warehouse context. A malicious or malformed file in the shared workspace could influence Roo Code’s tool use or instructions, while dbt-core’s outputs may be treated as trusted project artifacts. The shared filesystem bridge makes injection plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF Roo Code parses dbt-generated files or notes as instructions
IF MCP content is exposed through workspace artifacts
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Disable automatic parsing of workspace text as instructions
Require explicit human review before acting on file content
Use read-only mounts for dbt outputs where possible
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to workspace artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress; Roo Code reads workspace files, captures screens, and can call external model APIs. If warehouse-derived data is written into the shared workspace, Roo Code can ingest it and potentially transmit it to its configured model provider. The pair therefore creates a realistic leakage path in default workspace-sharing setups.
conditions: IF warehouse data is materialized into workspace files
IF Roo Code is configured with a third-party model API
IF screenshots or file contents include sensitive warehouse records
mitigations: Keep sensitive warehouse outputs out of the shared workspace
Use a local-only model backend for Roo Code
Redact secrets before writing dbt artifacts
Restrict workspace permissions to least privilege
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on workspace writes

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad workspace concurrency via filesystem; dbt-core also operates on project files and can emit artifacts into the same repo. Without locking, both agents can mutate the same files or git state, causing overwrites and inconsistent builds. The default shared-workspace model makes this a dangerous write-conflict pathway.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or workspace
IF git state is shared between their runs
IF no external locking or serialization is enforced
mitigations: Run the agents in separate branches
Serialize writes with a single-writer policy
Pause one agent while the other commits
Review diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can generate warehouse-facing outputs and Roo Code can act on workspace content with shell, git, and browser tools. If Roo Code treats dbt artifacts or summaries as authoritative, it may propagate a modeling mistake into commits or downstream actions. Because Roo Code has action-taking authority, the blast radius can extend beyond a single file.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes dbt outputs without verification
IF dbt artifacts are used as the basis for commits or browser actions
IF downstream automation trusts generated summaries
mitigations: Require human verification of dbt outputs
Add schema and test checks before Roo Code acts
Limit Roo Code to read-only review mode
Use signed artifacts for handoff
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while Roo Code handles workspace files, screenshots, and model-provider API keys. If regulated warehouse data or secrets are written into the workspace, Roo Code’s external API calls and screen capture can create retention and residency mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workspace
IF model-provider APIs retain prompts or screenshots
IF the warehouse data is subject to stricter residency or retention rules than the model backend
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Roo Code prompts
Disable screenshot sharing for sensitive sessions
Use a provider with compliant retention settings
Document data-flow boundaries
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
